h1: Sheet metal brakes and folding machines — box and pan, hand, magnetic, hydraulic, roofing and 3-in-1
intro: A sheet metal brake (folder) bends sheet by clamping it under a straight beam and swinging a folding leaf up around the edge — no punch and die, no marks on painted sheet, and long, straight bends in thin material that a press brake cannot hold flat. NovoTech sells six kinds in Canada, each on its own page: box and pan brakes with removable fingers for boxes and pans; straight hand brakes, foot-clamp folding machines and bench brakes for flashing, trim and duct; magnetic brakes that fold boxes of any depth; hydraulic, electric and CNC folding machines for 10 ga over 10 ft and production panels; portable roofing and siding brakes for the job site; and 3-in-1 shear, brake and roll machines for the small shop. Below, the six kinds compared, every one of the 137 models in one table, the questions we get asked and the buying guide. NovoTech's value-line brakes are built in China to our specification, with parts and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

faq.q: Box and pan brake, hand brake or magnetic brake — which do I need?
faq.a: A hand (straight) brake has a one-piece clamping blade: the best choice for long straight bends — flashing, trim, duct panels. A box and pan brake has a blade made of removable fingers, so it folds the four sides of a box or a pan; with all the fingers in it works as a straight brake too. A magnetic brake has no clamping beam at all — an electromagnet holds a loose steel bar on the sheet — so it folds boxes of any depth, closed and narrow shapes and short return flanges that a box and pan brake cannot reach, at the cost of a lower capacity (16 ga to 8 ft). For 14 ga and heavier, or for production, choose a hydraulic or electric folding machine.

faq.q: How are the capacities rated, and what about stainless and aluminum?
faq.a: Brake capacities are given in gauge of mild steel over the full bending length. Stainless steel bends at about two gauges lighter (a 16 ga brake takes 20 ga stainless), aluminum at about two gauges heavier. Bending at less than full length lets a brake take somewhat heavier sheet; folding heavier material than rated bends the beams permanently.

faq.q: Can a brake fold painted or coated sheet without marking it?
faq.a: Yes — that is one of the reasons to fold instead of press-brake bending. The sheet is clamped and the leaf swings around the clamp edge without sliding over a die. The ALB roofing brakes have a silicone insert in the bending beam for pre-painted coil and copper; on the other brakes a strip of protective film on the sheet keeps the finish perfect.

faq.q: When should I buy a hydraulic folding machine instead of a press brake?
faq.a: When the work is long panels in thin and medium sheet — duct, enclosures, architectural cladding, flashing — up to 10 ga. A folder bends from one side with the sheet lying flat, so a long panel needs no support or second person, there are no punch and die to change, and painted sheet is not marked. A press brake is the better machine for short heavy parts, for thick plate, for many different bends in one part and for tight tolerances on small flanges.

faq.q: What does a CNC folding machine add?
faq.a: A CNC folder (TFM, TFMS) positions the back gauge for every flange and folds to a programmed angle, one bend after the other from a program of up to 99 bends — the operator only turns and feeds the sheet. Programs are stored for repeat parts, the control corrects the angle for springback and folds radii in small steps. It pays for itself on production panels — cladding, cassettes, enclosures, duct — where a hand-set folder needs a skilled operator for every part. The TFMS has a segmented upper beam for boxes.

faq.q: What do I need to bend roofing flashing on site?
faq.a: A portable roofing brake: the ALB brakes have an aluminum frame on folding legs, set up in 10 – 15 minutes, take 24 ga steel and 0.032″ aluminum over 7.2 – 12.5 ft, bend to 180° and slit the coil with a roller knife. For the shop, a box and pan brake or a magnetic brake does the same work in heavier gauges.

faq.q: Do you still sell the brakes from the old website?
faq.a: The brakes on this page replace the earlier roofing and box and pan brakes. If you need parts or service for a brake you bought from NovoTech before, call us at 647-526-5510 with the model and serial number.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models with a small enough motor. Manual machines have no electrics.
